en: Analysis of the Bases of Psychic Power (Iddhipādavibhaṅga) 1.
The Exposition According to the Discourses (Suttantabhājanīya)
The four bases of psychic power:
here, a bhikkhu develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration of desire and volitional formations of striving;
he develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration of energy and volitional formations of striving.
He develops the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration of mind and volitional formations of striving;
he develops the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration of investigation and volitional formations of striving.
1.1. The Basis for Psychic Power through Desire.
And how does a bhikkhu develop the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration through desire and volitional formations of striving?
If a bhikkhu, having made desire dominant, attains concentration, attains one-pointedness of mind—
this is called "concentration through desire."
Thus, he generates desire, exerts himself, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states;
he generates desire, exerts himself, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states; [he generates desire] for the non-arising of unarisen...
He generates desire, exerts himself, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the arising of wholesome states; he generates desire,
exerts himself, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the stability, non-confusion, increase, expansion, development, and fulfillment of wholesome states that have already arisen.
These are called "volitional formations of striving.
Thus, this concentration through desire and these volitional formations of striving,
when taken together and condensed, come to be designated as "concentration through desire and volitional formations of striving."
In this context, what is zeal (*chanda*)?
That which is zeal, being zealous, the desire to act, wholesome zeal for the Dhamma—
this is called “zeal.”
In this context, what is concentration?

That which is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-dispersal, non-distraction, and state of mental non-distraction of the mind; serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration—this is called "concentration."
In this context, what is the volitional formation of striving?
It is that which is mental arousal of energy, exertion, endeavor, striving, effort, perseverance, fortitude, steadfastness, stability,
unflagging persistence, non-abandonment of zeal, non-abandonment of the burden, the grasping of the burden, energy, and vigor.
The faculty of energy, the power of energy, and right effort—
this is called the "volitional formation of striving.

Thus, he is endowed with, fully endowed with, has approached, fully approached, is possessed of, perfected in, and equipped with this desire, this concentration, and this volitional formation of striving.
Therefore it is said: “endowed with the volitional formations of striving associated with concentration through desire.

“Supernormal power” (*iddhi*) means: that which is the success, complete success, succeeding, complete succeeding, gain, acquisition, attainment, achievement, contact, realization, and fulfillment of those states.
“Basis of psychic power”:
for one who has become thus, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of volitional formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.
“He develops the basis of psychic power.”
He pursues, develops, and cultivates those qualities.
Therefore, it is said: "He develops the basis of psychic power.
1.2. The Basis of Psychic Power of Energy.
And how does a bhikkhu develop the basis for psychic power endowed with the volitional formation of energy and concentration?
When a bhikkhu, having made energy dominant, attains concentration, attains one-pointedness of mind—
this is called "energy-concentration."

Thus, he generates desire, exerts himself, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states; for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states; ... [and so on] ...
for the arising of unarisen wholesome states; ... [and so on] ...

He generates desire, exerts himself, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives for the stability, non-confusion, increase, abundance, development, and fulfillment of wholesome states that have arisen.
These are called "formations of striving.
Thus, there is this concentration through energy and these formations of striving.
Having gathered that together and condensed it, it is reckoned simply as the "volitional formation of energy and concentration.
In this context, what is energy?
It is the arousal of mental energy …pe… right effort.
This is called "energy.
In this context, what is concentration?

It is the stability, steadfastness, firm establishment, non-distraction, non-diffusion of the mind, the state of mental non-diffusion, serenity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, and right concentration.
This is called "concentration.
In that regard, what is the "volitional formation of striving"?
It is the arousal of mental energy, ... [as before] ... right effort.
This is called the "volitional formation of striving.
Thus, he is endowed with this energy, this concentration, and this volitional formation of striving... [as above] ...possessed of them.
Therefore, he is said to be "endowed with the volitional formation of striving for the sake of energy and concentration."

“Supernormal power” (*iddhi*) means: that which is the success, complete success, accomplishment, complete accomplishment, gain, acquisition, attainment, achievement, contact, realization, and fulfillment of those states.
“Basis of supernormal power” (*iddhipāda*) means: [the foundation for that].
For one who has become thus, there is the aggregate of feeling …pe… the aggregate of consciousness.
"He develops the basis of psychic power":
he pursues, develops, and cultivates those states.
Therefore it is said, “he develops the basis of psychic power.
1.3. The Basis of Psychic Power of Mind:
And how does a bhikkhu develop the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration of mind and volitional formations of striving?
If a bhikkhu, making the mind his dominant influence, attains concentration and attains one-pointedness of mind—
this is called "concentration of mind.
He generates desire and exerts effort for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states.
He arouses energy, exerts the mind, and strives for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states;
... [as before] ... for the arising of unarisen wholesome states; ... [as before] ...
and for the stability, non-confusion, increase, abundance, development, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states, he generates desire, makes an effort, arouses energy, exerts the mind, and strives.
These are called "volitional formations of striving.
Thus, this concentration of mind and these volitional formations of striving,
when taken together and condensed, come to be designated as "concentration of mind and volitional formations of striving."
In this context, what is consciousness (citta)?
That which is consciousness, mind, mentation …pe… the element of mind-consciousness born thereof—
this is called "consciousness."
In this context, what is concentration?
That which is the stability and steadfastness of the mind … [as far as] right concentration—
this is called “concentration.”
In this context, what is the volitional formation of striving?
That which is the arousal of mental energy, …pe… right effort—
this is called "the volitional formation of striving."
Thus, by means of this mind, this concentration, and this volitional formation of striving, he is endowed with them ... [and so on] ... possessed of them.
Therefore it is said: "endowed with the mental formation of concentration" (*cittasamādhipadhānasaṅkhārasamannāgata*). "Supernormal power" (*iddhi*)—thus it is called.
Whatever success, accomplishment, achievement, fulfillment, gain, acquisition, attainment, perfection, contact, realization, and mastery there is of those states—
that is the "basis of psychic power" (iddhipāda).
For one who has become thus, the aggregate of feeling … [and so on] … the aggregate of consciousness.
“He develops the basis for spiritual power”:
he pursues, develops, and cultivates those qualities.
Therefore it is said, “he develops the basis for spiritual power.”
1.4. The Basis of Psychic Power Consisting of Investigation And how does a bhikkhu develop the basis of psychic power endowed with the volitional formations of concentration due to investigation?
If, by making investigation the dominant factor, a bhikkhu gains concentration, gains one-pointedness of mind—
This is called "concentration through investigation.

For the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome states, he generates desire, exerts himself, arouses energy, applies his mind, and strives; for the abandoning of arisen evil, unwholesome states... [and so forth].

One generates desire, exerts oneself, arouses energy, applies the mind, and strives for the arising of unarisen wholesome states... [and so on] ...for the maintenance, non-confusion, increase, expansion, development, and fulfillment of arisen wholesome states.
These are called "volitional formations of striving."
Thus, this concentration through investigation and these volitional formations of striving,
when combined together and condensed, come to be designated simply as "concentration through investigation and volitional formations of striving.
In that regard, what is investigation?
That which is wisdom, understanding … [as before] … non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view—
this is called "investigation.
In this context, what is concentration?
That which is the stability, the steadfastness of the mind … right concentration—
this is called “concentration.
In this context, what is the volitional formation of striving?
That which is the mental arousal of energy … right effort—
this is called the "volitional formation of striving.
Thus, he is endowed with this inquiry, with this concentration, and with this volitional formation of striving … possessed of them.
Therefore it is said: "endowed with the volitional formations of striving associated with concentration through investigation.
"Supernormal power" (iddhi) refers to the success, complete success, accomplishment, achievement, gain, acquisition, attainment, fulfillment, contact, realization, and mastery regarding those states.
“Basis for spiritual power”:
the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of volitional formations, and the aggregate of consciousness belonging to one who has become such.
“He develops the basis for spiritual power.”
He pursues, develops, and cultivates those states.
Therefore it is said: "He develops the basis for psychic power.
This concludes the Exposition according to the Discourses (Suttantabhājanīya).
2. Analysis According to the Abhidhamma (Abhidhammabhājanīya):
The four bases of psychic power (iddhipādā).

Here, a bhikkhu develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration of will and volitional formations of striving; he develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration of energy and volitional formations of striving; he develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration of mind and volitional formations of striving; he develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration of investigation and volitional formations of striving.
He develops the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration of energy and volitional formations of striving;
he develops the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration of mind and volitional formations of striving;
he develops the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration of investigation and volitional formations of striving.

2.1. The Basis of Psychic Power Consisting of Zeal (Chandiddhipāda) And how does a bhikkhu develop the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration through zeal and volitional formations of striving?
Here, at whatever time a bhikkhu develops supramundane jhāna that is leading to liberation and conducive to the destruction of the acquisitions, [freeing him] from views...
For the sake of abandoning [the hindrances] and for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures...

he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge; at that time, he develops the basis of psychic power endowed with concentration of desire and volitional formations of striving.
In this context, what is desire?
Whatever is zeal, being zealous, the desire to act, and wholesome zeal for the Dhamma—
this is called "zeal.
In this context, what is concentration?

That which is the stability, the steadfastness of the mind... [as far as] right concentration, the concentration enlightenment factor, the path factor included in the path—this is called "concentration.
In this context, what is the volitional formation of striving?
That which is the mental arousal of energy … [as above] … right effort, the factor of enlightenment of energy, a factor of the path included within the path—
this is called the "volitional formation of striving.
Thus, he is endowed with this desire, this concentration, and this volitional formation of striving … [as above] … possessed of them.
Therefore it is said: “endowed with the volitional formations of striving associated with concentration through desire.

“Supernormal power” (*iddhi*) means: that which is the success, complete success, succeeding, complete succeeding, gain, acquisition, attainment, achievement, contact, realization, and fulfillment of those states.
“Basis of psychic power”:
for one who has become thus, there is contact ... [and so on] ... exertion and non-distraction.
“He develops the basis of psychic power.”
He pursues, develops, and cultivates those qualities.
Therefore it is said: "he develops the basis for psychic power.
2.2. The Basis for Psychic Power of Energy.
And how does a bhikkhu develop the basis for psychic power endowed with the concentration of energy and volitional formations of striving?

Here, at whatever time a bhikkhu develops supramundane jhāna that is leading to liberation, conducive to the removal of clinging, for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first stage—secluded from sensual pleasures... [as before] ...having entered upon the first jhāna.

He dwells in a practice that is painful and slow in direct knowledge; at that time, he develops the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration through energy and volitional formations of striving.
In this context, what is energy?
It is the arousal of mental energy … [as before] … right effort, the energy factor of enlightenment, a factor of the path, included within the path.
This is called "energy.
In this context, what is concentration?
That which is the stability and steadfastness of the mind... [as above] ...right concentration, the factor of enlightenment of concentration, a factor of the path, included within the path.
This is called “concentration.
In this context, what is the volitional formation of striving?
It is the arousal of mental energy … [as before] … right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a factor of the path, included within the path.
This is called the "volitional formation of striving.
Thus, he is endowed with this energy, this concentration, and this volitional formation of striving... [as before] ...possessed of them.
Therefore, he is said to be "endowed with energy, concentration, and the volitional formation of striving."

“Supernormal power” (*iddhi*) means: that which is the success, complete success, accomplishment, complete accomplishment, gain, acquisition, attainment, achievement, contact, realization, and fulfillment of those states.
“Basis of supernormal power” (*iddhipāda*) means: [the foundation for that].
For one who has become thus, there is contact... [and so on] ...exertion and non-distraction.
"He develops the basis for psychic power":
he pursues, develops, and cultivates those states.
Therefore it is said, “he develops the basis for psychic power.
2.3. The Basis for Psychic Power of Mind:
And how does a bhikkhu develop the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration of mind and volitional formations of striving?
Here, monks, at whatever time a monk develops supramundane jhāna, which leads to liberation, which leads to the waning of existence,
for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first stage— having detached from sensual pleasures... [as before] ...he enters and dwells in the first jhāna,
which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge— at that time he develops the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration of mind and volitional formations of striving.
In this context, what is consciousness (*citta*)?
That which is consciousness, mind (*mano*), mentation (*mānasa*) …pe… the element of mind-consciousness born thereof—
this is called "consciousness."
In this context, what is concentration?
That which is the stability and steadfastness of the mind … [as above] … right concentration, the factor of enlightenment of concentration, a factor of the path, included within the path—
this is called “concentration.”
In this context, what is the volitional formation of striving?
That which is the arousal of mental energy … [as above] … right effort, the factor of enlightenment of energy, a factor of the path included within the path—
this is called the volitional formation of striving.
Thus, by means of this mind, this concentration, and this volitional formation of striving, he is endowed with them ... [as before] ... possessed of them.
Therefore it is said: "endowed with the volitional formation of striving for concentration of mind.
"Supernormal power" (iddhi).

That which is the success, the complete success, the succeeding, the complete succeeding, the gain, the obtaining, the attainment, the achievement, the reaching, the realization, the fulfillment, and the acquisition of those states—this is called "the basis of psychic power" (*iddhipāda*).
For one who has become thus, there is contact... [and so on] ...exertion and non-distraction.
“He develops the basis for spiritual power”:
he pursues, develops, and cultivates those states.
Therefore it is said, “he develops the basis for spiritual power.”
2.4. The Basis of Psychic Power Consisting in Investigation And how does a bhikkhu develop the basis of psychic power endowed with the volitional formations of concentration due to investigation?
Here, at whatever time a bhikkhu develops supramundane jhāna that is leading to liberation and conducive to the destruction of clinging, [free from] views...
For the sake of abandoning [the hindrances] and for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures...

he enters and dwells in the first *jhāna*, which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge. At that time, he develops the basis of psychic power (*iddhipāda*) endowed with the concentration of investigation and volitional formations of striving.
In this context, what is investigation?

That wisdom which is understanding … [as above] … non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a factor of the path, included within the path—
this is called "investigation.
In this context, what is concentration?
That which is the stability and steadfastness of the mind … right concentration, the concentration factor of enlightenment, the path factor included in the path—
this is called “concentration.
In this context, what is the volitional formation of striving?
Whatever mental application of energy... [as above] ...right effort, the energy factor of enlightenment, a path constituent included in the path—this is called the "volitional formation of striving.
Thus, he is endowed with, fully endowed with, arrived at, fully arrived at, possessed of, perfected in, and equipped with this inquiry, this concentration, and this volitional formation of striving.
Therefore it is said: "Endowed with the volitional formations of striving for concentration through investigation" is "supernormal power" (iddhi).
That which is the success, complete success, accomplishment, achievement, gain, acquisition, attainment, fulfillment, contact, realization, and full realization of those states.
“Basis of psychic power”:
for one who has become thus, there is contact … [and so on] … exertion and non-distraction.
“He develops the basis of psychic power.”
One cultivates, develops, and frequently practices those states.
Therefore, it is said: "one develops the basis for psychic power.
There are four bases for psychic power:

The basis of psychic power consisting of desire, the basis of psychic power consisting of energy, the basis of psychic power consisting of consciousness, and the basis of psychic power consisting of investigation.
Therein, what is the basis of psychic power consisting of desire?
Here, at whatever time a bhikkhu develops supramundane jhāna that is leading to liberation and conducive to the destruction of the acquisitions, [freeing him] from views...
For the sake of abandoning [the hindrances] and for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures...

one enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge; at that time, whatever desire, longing, wish-to-act, and wholesome desire for the Dhamma there is—this is [the faculty of desire].
This is called the "basis of psychic power consisting of desire.
The remaining factors are associated with the basis of psychic power consisting of desire.
In this context, what is the "basis of psychic power consisting of energy"?

Here, bhikkhu, at whatever time a bhikkhu develops supramundane jhāna that leads to liberation, conduces to the waning of existence, and is for the abandoning of views and the attainment of the first stage—being secluded from sensual pleasures...

[as before] ...he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge—at that time, there is the arousal of mental energy... [as before] ... *Note: The ellipses (... indicate the omission of the standard formula for the first jhāna.*
Right effort, the energy factor of enlightenment, a factor of the path included in the path—
this is called the "basis of psychic power consisting of energy.
All remaining phenomena are associated with the basis of psychic power consisting of energy.
In this context, what is the basis of psychic power consisting of concentration of mind?

Here, at whatever time a bhikkhu develops supramundane jhāna that leads to liberation and results in the diminution of existence, for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first stage—secluded from sensual pleasures... [and so on] ...having attained the first jhāna.
He dwells in a practice that is painful with sluggish direct knowledge; at that time, whatever is mind, intellect, mentation … [as before] … the corresponding mind-consciousness element—
this is called the basis of psychic power consisting of mind.
The remaining factors are associated with the basis of psychic power that is investigation.
In this context, what is the basis of psychic power that is investigation?
Here, at whatever time a bhikkhu develops supramundane jhāna that is leading to liberation and conducive to the destruction of acquisitions, [free from] views...
For the sake of abandoning [the hindrances] and for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures...
he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge. At that time, whatever wisdom there is, which is understanding...
non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment, a factor of the path, included within the path—this is [wisdom].
This is called the "basis of accomplishment through investigation.
All remaining phenomena are associated with the basis of accomplishment through investigation.
This concludes the *Abhidhammabhājanīya*.
3. Interrogation on Questions.
The four bases for psychic power:

here, a bhikkhu develops the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration due to desire and volitional formations of striving; [he develops] the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration due to energy … [and so on].

He develops the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration of mind and volitional formations of striving …pe… the basis for psychic power endowed with concentration of investigation and volitional formations of striving.
Of the four bases for psychic power, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many indeterminate …pe… how many with conflict, how many without conflict?
3.1. The Triads.
Only wholesome [states].
They may be associated with pleasant feeling, or they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
States that are subject to ripening.
Not grasped and not conducive to grasping.
Not defiled and not subject to defilement.
They may be with applied thought and sustained thought; they may be without applied thought and with sustained thought only; or they may be without applied thought and without sustained thought.
They may be accompanied by rapture, accompanied by pleasure, or accompanied by equanimity.
They are not to be abandoned either by vision or by cultivation.
Those whose roots are to be abandoned neither by vision nor by cultivation;
those leading to the diminution [of existence]; those in training (sekha).
Infinite.
Having an infinite object.
Exalted.
Regarding the state of being fixed in rightness (*sammattaniyatā*):
it does not have the Path as its object (*ārammaṇa*), it has the Path as its cause (*hetu*), but it does not have the Path as its predominance (*adhipati*).
It may be arisen, or it may be unarisen; it should not be said that it is "bound to arise."
It may be past, it may be future, or it may be present.
It should not be said that its object is past, nor that its object is future, nor that its object is present.
It may be internal, it may be external, or it may be both internal and external.
Having external objects.
Invisible and non-reacting.
3.2. 3.2 Duka (Pairs)
3.2.1. The Section on Causes (Hetugocchaka).
The basis for spiritual power consisting of investigation is a cause; the other three bases for spiritual power are not causes.
They are accompanied by causes.
Associated with causes.

The basis of psychic power consisting of investigation is both a cause and accompanied by a cause; the other three bases of psychic power cannot be said to be "both causes and accompanied by causes," but they are accompanied by causes and are not themselves causes.

The basis of psychic power consisting of investigation is both a cause and associated with a cause; the other three bases of psychic power cannot be said to be "both causes and associated with causes," but they are associated with causes and are not themselves causes.

Three bases of psychic power are not roots, yet they are accompanied by roots. The basis of psychic power consisting of investigation should not be described as "not a root, yet accompanied by a root," nor as "not a root, yet without a root.
9.3.2.2. The Minor Intermediate Couplets, etc.:
They possess conditions.
Conditioned.
Non-manifesting.
Non-reactive.
Formless.
Supramundane.
Cognizable by some, not cognizable by others.
Without taints.
Untainted. Dissociated from taints.
They should not be described as both taints (*āsava*) and associated with taints; nor should they be described as associated with taints but not being taints themselves.
They should not be described as both taints and associated with taints; nor should they be described as associated with taints but not being taints themselves.
They are dissociated from taints and are not taints.
There are no fetters … [as before] … no ties … [as before] … no floods … [as before].
There are no yokes … and so on … no hindrances … and so on … no misapprehensions … and so on …
They have an object.
Three bases of psychic power are not consciousness; the base of psychic power consisting of consciousness is consciousness.
Three bases of psychic power are mental factors; the base of psychic power consisting of consciousness is not a mental factor.

Three bases of psychic power are associated with consciousness; the base of psychic power that is consciousness itself cannot be said to be either "associated with consciousness" or "dissociated from consciousness.

Three bases of psychic power are conjoined with consciousness; the base of psychic power that is consciousness itself cannot be said to be either "conjoined with consciousness" or "disjoined from consciousness.
Three bases of psychic power are generated by consciousness; the base of psychic power that is consciousness itself is not generated by consciousness.
Three bases of psychic power are co-existent with consciousness; the base of psychic power consisting of consciousness is not co-existent with consciousness.
Three bases of psychic power follow after consciousness; the base of psychic power consisting of consciousness does not follow after consciousness.
Three bases of psychic power are conjoined with and produced by consciousness; the base of psychic power consisting of consciousness is neither conjoined with nor produced by consciousness.

Three bases of psychic power are conjoined with, originated by, and co-existent with the mind; the base of psychic power consisting of mind is not conjoined with, originated by, or co-existent with the mind.

Three bases of psychic power follow after what is conjoined with and originated by the mind; the base of psychic power consisting of mind does not follow after what is conjoined with and originated by the mind.
Three bases of psychic power are external; the base of psychic power consisting of mind is internal.
9.3.2.11. The Group on Grasping (Upādānagocchaka), etc.:
Not grasped; not clung to.
There are no clingings …pe… no defilements …pe… they are not to be abandoned by vision.
Not to be abandoned by cultivation.
Not having roots to be abandoned by vision.
Not having roots to be abandoned by cultivation.
They may be with applied thought, or they may be without applied thought.
They may be with sustained thought, or they may be without sustained thought.
They may be accompanied by rapture, or they may be without rapture.
It may be accompanied by rapture, or it may not be accompanied by rapture.
It may be accompanied by pleasure, or it may not be accompanied by pleasure.
It may be accompanied by equanimity, or it may not be accompanied by equanimity.
Neither belonging to the sense sphere,
nor belonging to the fine-material sphere,
nor belonging to the immaterial sphere.
Unincluded.
Leading out.
Certain.
The Unsurpassed.
The Non-conflict.
The Interrogation on Questions.
The Analysis of the Bases of Psychic Power is finished.
